content.title: About
content.content: Toasted sour‑dough bread is made from whole‑grain flour, water, salt and a natural starter. Baking creates a crisp crust and a soft, aromatic crumb with a subtle tang.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The starter contains live lactic‑acid bacteria that enhance flavor and extend shelf life.
Toasting triggers the Maillard reaction, giving the bread nutty notes and a golden color.
Traditional sour‑dough bread is leavened without commercial yeast, making it a more natural product.
In many cultures toasted sour‑dough is served with olive oil or avocado for breakfast.
Sour‑dough bread has a lower glycemic index than bread made with rapid‑rise yeast.

items.title: Rich in probiotics
items.content: Live bacteria from the starter support a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Whole‑grain flour provides sustained energy and prolonged satiety.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: B1, B2 and B3 aid metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Provides minerals
items.content: Magnesium, iron and zinc in the bread contribute to muscle and immune health.

items.title: Low in added sugar
items.content: Absence of added sugars makes it suitable for moderate consumption.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Wheat‑based bread contains gluten, which can trigger reactions in people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Toasting reduces moisture, increasing calorie density; portion control is advised.

items.title: Salt content
items.content: The salt used in the recipe may be a concern for individuals monitoring blood pressure.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Toasted sour‑dough bread is perfect for sandwiches, avocado toast, croutons, or as a side to salads. It can be spread with olive oil, butter, or low‑fat cheese.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the bread in a paper bag or bread box at room temperature for up to 3 days. For longer storage, wrap tightly in foil and refrigerate (up to 1 week) or freeze (up to 3 months). Reheat in a toaster before serving.
